title: SIU clears officer in cellblock injury
article: A Windsor cop won't be held criminally responsible for a serious brain injury that sent a man in police custody to hospital, the province's civilian police watchdog has concluded.
"It's clear that there's no reasonable grounds to believe that the officer committed any criminal offence," said Rose Bliss, a spokeswoman for the Special Investigations Unit.
On Oct. 19 around 5:30 p.m. two officers arrested a 44-year-old man for public intoxication outside the West-Court Building at 251 Goyeau St.

Less than 11 hours later an officer monitoring the man's holding cell noticed he was semi-conscious. The inmate was rushed to Hotel- Dieu Grace Hospital where he underwent surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain.

In the course of their probe, the SIU viewed a police booking room videotape which revealed a brief tussle between the man and an officer. The footage shows the man shoving the officer, the officer pushing back and the man stumbling before striking his head on an elevated desk counter.
"The blow caused no noticeable physical injury to the man," a summary of the SIU's report says.
The SIU determined the man suffered at least two serious blows to his head Oct. 19. Both occurred before his arrest.
However, investigators were stymied when the man refused to release his medical records -- they couldn't pinpoint precisely which blow caused his head trauma.

"The complainant in this case suffered a significant internal injury as a result of some incident but what that incident is remains a mystery," concluded SIU director James Cornish. He went on to say that even if the injury in the booking room prompted the man's brain bleed, "there appears to be no intent on the part of the officer to injure the man."
When the SIU began examining the case it posted flyers inviting witnesses to the Goyeau Street arrest to come forward.
"We did get several civilian witnesses that came forward because of our appeal," said Bliss. "As far as we know the evidence indicates the man was arrested on Goyeau Street without incident."

Neither the SIU nor Windsor police would release the 44-year- old's name Friday. The name of the officer involved in the booking room scuffle is also being kept under wraps, Bliss said, because the SIU only releases a cop's name if criminal charges are laid.
Windsor police Insp. Dave Perpich, who runs the force's detention unit, welcomed word the officer had been cleared of wrongdoing.
"According to the investigation and with the information we had, I'm not surprised at the finding that the officer was not criminally responsible," he said.
SIU investigations are conducted whenever a civilian is killed or seriously injured either by police or while in police custody.
